sources.note: Introduces a counterfactual intervention framework to test whether large reasoning models' intermediate thinking-draft steps and final answers are causally faithful to each other, finding they often are not.
sources.title: Measuring the Faithfulness of Thinking Drafts in Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: Identifies an implicit first-guess bias formed on reading a question as a causal driver of overthinking in reasoning models, verified through counterfactual interventions and attention analysis.
sources.title: The First Impression Problem: Internal Bias Triggers Overthinking in Reasoning Models

sources.note: Introduces RFEval, a benchmark that uses counterfactual interventions to test whether an LRM's stated chain-of-thought causally drives its answer, finding 49.7% of outputs unfaithful.
sources.title: RFEval: Benchmarking Reasoning Faithfulness under Counterfactual Reasoning Intervention in Large Reasoning Models

result.definition: A causal-analysis technique that alters part of a reasoning trace (e.g. an intermediate thinking-draft step, or a model's implicit first guess) and observes whether the final answer changes, to test whether that part actually drove the outcome rather than being post-hoc narration. Used in the archive to test chain-of-thought faithfulness (Measuring the Faithfulness of Thinking Drafts, RFEval) and to establish that an implicit first-guess bias causally triggers overthinking (The First Impression Problem).
